title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor
talk_summary: Charlie Holtz (Conductor) shares principles from watching top builders manage teams of coding agents: stay near but not at the frontier, protect critical code with human review, centralize all org context in a queryable database, and run agents in persistent cloud sandboxes rather than on laptops. The core thesis is that agents should be orchestrated like an orchestra (human zooming in/out over parallel agent work) rather than run as an automated factory.

takeaways.technique: Slop-free zones with mandatory human review
takeaways.what_they_do: Designate specific files/areas (migrations, docs, skill files) where AI changes require strict human review, while being deliberately loose elsewhere; enforce via CI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any change to migrations file requires the AI uh a human to review it

takeaways.technique: Invest heavily in agent instruction files (CLAUDE.md/skills)
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the always-loaded agent context file like whispering guidance to a new intern every day, and spend unusual time making it high quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they put an unusual amount of time into the cloud MD or their skill files

takeaways.technique: Centralized org context DB with SQL access ('feed the beast')
takeaways.what_they_do: Pipe Slack messages, Discord bug reports, and meeting recordings into a Postgres table and give agents a SQL tool to query it all.
takeaways.evidence_quote: put everything in a database and then give your agent a SQL tool and let it handle

takeaways.what_they_do: Move agent workspaces from local git worktrees to cloud sandboxes so runs survive laptop closure and can run long/hard tasks without being killed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can close my laptop and the agents are going to keep running

takeaways.technique: Agent-spawning API for self-service work creation
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose an orchestration API so an agent (or human via chat) can create new workspaces/tasks programmatically, kicking off work remotely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Lord Crandon has access to the conductor API and so can kick off work itself

takeaways.technique: Don't beat the market — avoid over-optimizing workflows without proprietary alpha
takeaways.what_they_do: Before investing in a custom workflow, ask 'why isn't this the default?' and only build custom when you have real alpha (info about your users/codebase models lack).
takeaways.evidence_quote: unless you have like real alpha you shouldn't be optimizing your workflow too much
